title: The degree of the dictionary
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve ([def-pc-smooth-projective-curve])
which is geometrically irreducible, hence geometrically integral with
$H^0(X,\cO_X)=k$ (this is needed: for $X=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf C}$ over
$k=\mathbf R$ and $K=\mathbf C$ the conclusion fails),
of genus $g$ ([def-pc-genus]) and $\cL$ an invertible sheaf (line
bundle) on the base change $X_K$ ([def-pc-base-change], [def-sc-invertible-module])
for a field extension $K/k$ ([def-pc-field-extension]), with $h^0(X_K,\cL)=1$
and $H^q(X_K,\cL)=0$ for $q>0$. Then

$$
\deg(\cL)=\chi(\cL)-\chi(\cO_{X_K})=1-(1-g)=g.
$$

This is the exact instance of Riemann–Roch used in the
zero-scheme dictionary ([lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd]).

proof.text: By the definition of the Euler characteristic as the alternating sum of the finite-dimensional cohomology groups, the hypotheses $h^0(X_K,\cL)=1$ and $H^q(X_K,\cL)=0$ for every $q>0$ give $\chi(X_K,\cL)=1$.

The field extension $K/k$ is flat and $X$ is proper over $k$, so flat cohomology base change applied to the structure sheaf gives $H^i(X_K,\cO_{X_K})\cong H^i(X,\cO_X)\otimes_k K$ for all $i\ge0$. For $i=0$ this is $H^0(X,\cO_X)\otimes_k K=K$, using the hypothesis $H^0(X,\cO_X)=k$. For $i\ge2$ the cohomology of the smooth projective curve $X$ vanishes, hence so does $H^i(X_K,\cO_{X_K})$. The genus base-change statement (whose hypotheses, $X$ geometrically irreducible with $H^0(X,\cO_X)=k$, are those of the item) gives $\dim_K H^1(X_K,\cO_{X_K})=g(X)=g$. Thus the alternating sum defining the Euler characteristic is $\chi(X_K,\cO_{X_K})=1-g$.
By the definition of the degree of an invertible sheaf, $\deg(\cL)=\chi(X_K,\cL)-\chi(X_K,\cO_{X_K})$. Substituting the two preceding computations gives $\deg(\cL)=1-(1-g)=g$.
